(1) DNNs prefer to focus on easy-to-learn cues and (2) the abundance of certain solutions in the parameter space is explained by their descriptional complexity.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: which cues will DNNs prefer? Our results show that DNNs tend to choose the cues that are simple to describe.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNNs are biased toward easy–to–understand cues, which is a result of the abundance of solutions in the parameter space corresponding to those simple cues.
DNNs prefer to choose simple cues, and that the abundance of simple solutions is the main cause of shortcut learning.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inborn biases of DNNs are more complex and more difficult to eliminate than we thought.
the shortcut cues are abundant in parameter space, and the DNNs will choose the simple ones.
shortcut learning is not a mere problem of the current DNNs, but also a fundamental property of the parameter spaces of DNNs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parameter space is the key to understand the behavior of DNNs.
shortcut learning, which is a major limitation in DNNs, is not only a problem of the current generation, but also a fundamental limitation in DNN-based machine learning.
, when designing DNNs, we must be aware of the fact that models are prone to learn easy–to–discover cues, even when those cues may not be essential for the task at hand.
